name: Z-Press with Dumbbells (Neutral Grip)
description: The dumbbell neutral-grip Z-press is performed seated on the floor with legs extended, pressing dumbbells overhead with palms facing each other. The floor-seated position eliminates leg drive and forces upright torso posture via hamstring and hip flexor flexibility demands. The neutral grip is more comfortable for many trainees than the standard pronated Z-press grip, reducing wrist and elbow stress while maintaining the same shoulder loading pattern.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the floor with legs fully extended straight in front. Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with a neutral (hammer) grip. Sit upright — torso perpendicular to the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: If hamstring tightness prevents an upright torso, perform with a slight back support initially. Moderate weight — the floor position eliminates leg drive entirely.
steps: Step 1: Begin seated upright on the floor, dumbbells at shoulder height neutral grip.
Step 2: Press both dumbbells overhead, maintaining neutral wrist position.
Step 3: At full lockout, shrug the traps slightly into the top position.
Step 4: Lower under control back to shoulder level.
Step 5: Maintain upright torso throughout — no leaning back.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale pressing. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Leaning back as the press becomes difficult — the upright position is non-negotiable
Feet rotating or legs lifting — legs stay flat on the floor
safety_considerations: Adequate hamstring flexibility required — do not force a rounded-back position
Build up load slowly — no leg drive means lower absolute loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder height to full overhead lockout.
